viability: Three directly inspected sources support a modest, substantive article about the recorded weaving name, regional labels and changes in work. They do not establish a single founder, earliest-ever date, complete branch map or common ancestry. Build around Bhadrak Aswini Tanti and one explicitly identified Bomkai Patra Tanti weaver; exclude Pantanti/Pana Tanti evidence from the article body unless discussing why it is a separate unresolved scope.

sources.title: A. Stirling, An account, geographical, statistical and historical of Orissa Proper or Cuttack (1825), excerpt in Report on the Population Estimates of India (1820–1830)
sources.publication: Census of India1961 series, edited Durgaprasad Bhattacharya and Bibhavati Bhattacharya; Office of Registrar General, Ministry of Home Affairs; foreword dated8January1963.
sources.locator: Printed169/PDF213 identifies original source/1825; printed172/PDF216 table headed Ooria/Sanscrit/Occupations.
sources.claims: The table pairs Tanti with Tantravaya and Weaver. This establishes a dated nineteenth-century use in an account of Orissa Proper/Cuttack, not an origin date. The same page contains trade-origin stories and caste hierarchy; these are the author's transmitted classifications and beliefs, not proof of human rank or ancestry. It lists other cloth-related names separately, so an occupational field need not be a single community.

limits: Reject caste-rank and mixed-descent mythology as factual genealogy.
Do not identify1825as earliest-ever use or date of community creation.
No linguistic derivation of modern Odia spelling established from this table.

sources.title: Odisha District Gazetteers: Bhadrak
sources.publisher: Gopabandhu Academy of Administration, General Administration Department, Government of Odisha; Chief Editor DrTaradatt
sources.locator: Printed38–39/PDF54–55, Castes: Aswini Tanti; printed10/PDF26 distinguishes weaving Tanti and cloth-trading Kapudia; frontmatteriii–iv compilation2015–16.
sources.claims: The Aswini Tanti entry describes an inherited weaving occupation followed by movement into agriculture and other work over the preceding century. It attributes that change to colonial promotion of imported cloth and restrictions on handlooms. Treat the causal argument as the gazetteer's retrospective explanation; no supporting household time series or specific regulations are supplied there. The account is useful because community history can persist after the old occupation changes, and because it names a particular regional label rather than all Odisha weavers.
sources.strength: Original institutional district account, compiled2015–16; exact publication date unresolved.
limits: Do not repeat its blanket claim of lost skill as true of every present family.
Do not derive population numbers from vague huge population statements.
Aswini Tanti is the source's spelling; not exhaustive branch map.
Do not claim all modern Tantis descend from the district group.

sources.title: Gunjan Jain, Why Are We So Determined to Deny Indians the Cloth They Prefer?
sources.publication: Global InCH International Journal of Intangible Cultural Heritage, January2015
sources.inspection: Original publicly accessible preview downloaded and read. Body ends after opening paragraphs; subscription remainder not accessed.
sources.locator: Opening four preview paragraphs, named Kabiraj at Bomkai village.
sources.claims: Jain identifies Kabiraj as Patra Tanti and Vaishnav, working a pit loom in the front room of his Bomkai home. She describes a regular sari taking7–10days, greater time for elaborate silk work, yarn prices rising faster than earnings and migration among other village weavers. The account gives inherited craft a human setting and economic conditions, while showing that continuing to weave involves choice and viable work. These are2015reported conditions, not present prices or a survey of every Tanti family.
sources.strength: Original named craft-worker account by textile practitioner, limited to accessible preview.
limits: Source calls location Berhampur district; avoid reproducing that administrative imprecision. Use Bomkai village, Odisha, or separately sourced Ganjam location.
Do not reproduce last-four count as current fact.
No caste inferred from Kabiraj's name: identity explicitly stated by source.
No photograph reuse licence established; link source rather than copying images.
Specific Patra Tanti identification is not proof of equivalence with Pana/Pantanti.
